title.value: Handling Black Swan Events in Deep Learning with Diversely Extrapolated Neural Networks
title.justification: The title is explicitly provided in the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: To avoid this pitfall, we introduce DENN, an ensemble approach building a set of Diversely Extrapolated Neural Networks...

analysis.description: This paper introduces DENN, an ensemble approach to improve prediction uncertainty in neural networks when encountering out-of-distribution (OOD) data, commonly referred to as black swan events. The method involves adding a diversity term in the loss function and is tested on regression, classification, and safe imitation learning tasks.

type.justification: The paper describes empirical experiments and comparisons of the proposed method with existing approaches on regression, classification, and safe imitation learning tasks.
type.quote: An empirical study of the proposed approach applied to NNs on regression, classification and anomaly detection for safe imitation learning tasks (Sec. 4).

name.justification: The primary focus of the research is on estimating and handling predictive uncertainty in neural networks, particularly in the context of unexpected or 'black swan' events.
name.quote: ...models tend to be extremely “surprised” by rare events, leading to potentially disastrous consequences...

name.justification: The research heavily focuses on ensemble methods to improve uncertainty estimation.
name.quote: Ensembles of NNs are a useful solution to this issue. They are a collection of several NNs, each initialized differently.

name.justification: The paper discusses the application of the method to anomaly detection in classification tasks.
name.quote: Then, we show how the loss can be adapted to tackle anomaly detection during classification, as well as safe imitation learning problems.

name.justification: Safe imitation learning tasks are mentioned as one of the application areas for the proposed method.
name.quote: Then, we show how the loss can be adapted to tackle anomaly detection during classification, as well as safe imitation learning problems.

name.justification: DENN is the central model proposed in the paper to address the problem of uncertainty in deep learning.
name.quote: To avoid this pitfall, we introduce DENN, an ensemble approach building a set of Diversely Extrapolated Neural Networks...

is_contributed.justification: The paper introduces DENN as a new approach to address black swan events in deep learning.
is_contributed.quote: The main contributions of this work are: • A novel way to enforce diversity in ensembles...

is_executed.justification: The paper mentions experiments and evaluations carried out using DENN on different tasks.
is_executed.quote: In this section, we apply the proposed loss function to different tasks and compare the results...

is_compared.justification: DENN is compared to existing ensemble methods across various experiments in the paper.
is_compared.quote: We compare DENN (Alg. 1) with popular ensemble methods: anchoring [Pearce et al., 2018], input bootstrap [Efron, 1982], bootstrap prior [Osband et al., 2018] and MC dropout [Gal and Ghahramani, 2016].

referenced_paper_title.justification: Since DENN is introduced in this paper, there is no prior reference paper dedicated solely to it.

name.justification: MNIST is used as a benchmark dataset for evaluating classification tasks.
name.quote: We also compare ourselves to Outlier Exposure (OE) using the authors’ code to train a single MLP constrained to output uniform predictions OOD (also accessed using an external dataset).
